name: Surface Chemistry
tagline: Adsorption, thin films, and interfacial phenomena at surfaces.
seo_title: Surface Chemistry — paper summaries, news & innovations | Chemisters
seo_description: Follow Chemisters Surface Chemistry on LinkedIn and Facebook: paper summaries, news and innovations in adsorption, interfaces, thin films, wetting and surface analysis.

definition.lead: Surface chemistry studies what happens at the boundary between two phases: solid and gas, solid and liquid, liquid and gas.
definition.body: Catalysis, corrosion, adhesion, lubrication, cleaning, sensors and chip manufacturing all happen at surfaces. A few atomic layers often decide how a whole material behaves.

timeline.title: Oil calms water
timeline.text: Benjamin Franklin reports how a spoonful of oil spreads over a pond.
timeline.why: An early clue to molecular-scale films.

timeline.title: Young's equation
timeline.text: Thomas Young relates the contact angle of a droplet to surface tensions.

timeline.title: Measuring surface films
timeline.text: Agnes Pockels publishes surface tension measurements made with a trough she built at home.

timeline.title: Monolayers
timeline.text: Irving Langmuir shows that films on water can be one molecule thick.
timeline.why: Molecules at surfaces can be counted and measured.

timeline.title: The Langmuir isotherm
timeline.text: Langmuir models monolayer adsorption on surfaces.
timeline.why: Still the starting model for adsorption.

timeline.title: Nobel Prize
timeline.text: Irving Langmuir receives the Nobel Prize for discoveries in surface chemistry.

timeline.title: BET theory
timeline.text: Brunauer, Emmett and Teller model multilayer adsorption.
timeline.why: The standard way to measure surface area.

timeline.title: Seeing surfaces atom by atom
timeline.text: The scanning tunnelling microscope is invented.
timeline.why: Surfaces could be imaged at atomic resolution.

timeline.title: The lotus effect
timeline.text: Wilhelm Barthlott and Christoph Neinhuis explain the self-cleaning lotus leaf.

timeline.title: Surface reactions explained
timeline.text: Gerhard Ertl receives the Nobel Prize for studies of chemical processes on solid surfaces.

quiz.q: How does adsorption differ from absorption?
options: Adsorption happens on a surface; absorption happens into the bulk
They are the same process with two names
Adsorption needs a liquid to happen
quiz.explain: A sponge absorbs; activated carbon adsorbs.

options: A single layer of adsorption on identical sites
Unlimited layers of molecules stacking up
Only liquids can adsorb on surfaces
quiz.explain: Coverage saturates when every site is filled.

quiz.q: The BET method is used to measure…
options: The surface area of porous solids
quiz.explain: From how much nitrogen gas adsorbs at low temperature.
They crowd at the surface and weaken water's cohesion there.

quiz.q: A water contact angle above 150° means a surface is…
quiz.explain: Droplets bead up and roll off.

options: Physisorption is weak van der Waals binding; chemisorption forms chemical bonds
They are the same process at different temperatures
Adsorbing them on its huge internal surface
Reacting them with water inside the pores
quiz.explain: A gram can have over 1,000 m² of surface.

quiz.q: Why are surface atoms more reactive than bulk atoms?
options: They have fewer neighbours and unsatisfied bonds
quiz.explain: That is why finely divided metals are good catalysts.

quiz.q: Gerhard Ertl's 2007 Nobel Prize was for…
